scope: Current factual research package for the members-only Fishing skilling boss at Tempoross Cove. It proposes integration records only. It neither alters shared production data nor assigns route order, target permit count, success, rewards, collection-log state, attention preference, or a stop condition.

included: current access, transport, local tools, round phases, attacks, contribution points, permit threshold, reward-pool mechanics, and repeatability
deterministic versus RNG boundaries for rewards, Fishing-level reward brackets, duplicate replacement, and item utility
factual alternatives for harpooning, cooking, tethering, fire control, local item recovery, and travel
proposed observed account state for attempts, point/permit deltas, pool balance, searches, unique items, and temporary minigame supplies
excluded: whether Tempoross should be rushed, played solo rather than in a group, or completed to any particular Fishing level, permit count, or collection-log state
any assumed successful game, points, permits, searches, catches, supplies, XP, unique drop, reward-pool result, or player readiness
execution-dependent XP, permits, rewards, attention intervals, money, food, or time-per-hour estimates
community solo rotations and stopping targets, except as explicitly labeled strategy candidates

minigame_gate.boostability: The activity lists level 35 Fishing as its only gate. Treat entry as requiring an observed current eligible Fishing level; do not infer it from XP, a planned boost, or earlier participation.

location_and_transport: Board at the sea-spirit dock west of the Ruins of Unkah, then sail to Tempoross Cove. Desert heat remains a travel consideration until reaching the relevant safe area; it is not a minigame combat requirement.
Direct: Ferryman Sathwood south of Al Kharid bank travels to the destination.
Near: Pharaoh's sceptre Jaldraocht teleport then travel south-west; Camulet Enakhra's Temple Entrance then travel south; magic carpet to Menaphos then travel north-west.

Sailing alternative: dock at Ruins of Unkah with observed Sailing level 48 and an independently observed vessel/docking capability. This package does not infer the vessel, route, or dock availability.

Return/reward location: the Reward pool is in the Ruins of Unkah immediately outside the bank. Successful encounters return there automatically after a short delay, with a local leave option as an alternative.

facts: A player boards one of two functionally equivalent ships and arrives at the Cove.
Cove crates provide basic ropes, buckets, hammers, and harpoons when forgotten or lost.
Players may start a solo instance from the rope ladder or join a group encounter; choice does not itself establish a successful encounter.
Fish harpoonfish from cove spots. Jumping spots can produce two harpoonfish at once; catches are still variable and must be observed.
Raw harpoonfish drain 10 Tempoross energy when fired by cannon; cooked harpoonfish drain 15.
Load harpoonfish into cannon ammunition crates, then fire cannons to reduce Tempoross energy.
Energy naturally returns during the encounter. Storm intensity changes as the fight progresses and drives attack pressure; no player-specific intensity progress may be inferred.
At zero energy, Tempoross submerges and spirit pools appear. Harpoon energised fish from a spirit pool to scatter essence.
The max hit against a spirit pool is 12 regardless of Fishing level. Successful scatter messages restore 3 percent run energy at the stated interval.
Solo and group player counts change the total essence available; a group or solo label is not enough to infer an exact essence total or personal contribution.
Repeat energy-drain and vulnerable phases until Tempoross essence is reduced to zero for success.
If the encounter succeeds, the player is returned to Ruins of Unkah after a short delay or can use the local leave option.
Failure does not create a player death by default, but earned encounter points are lost and no permit is awarded from that failed encounter.

energy_and_contribution.fishing_and_cooking: Fishing harpoonfish awards 5 contribution points per fish. Cooking awards 10 per fish. A capture, cooking event, XP amount, or inventory count is never inferred.
energy_and_contribution.cannon_loading: Depositing raw, cooked, or crystallised harpoonfish awards 20, 65, or 20 contribution points respectively. Raw and cooked fish have 10 and 15 cannon-energy damage respectively.
energy_and_contribution.support_actions: Repairing a mast or totem awards 40 points and Construction XP equal to four times the player's Construction level. Dousing one fire awards 40 points. Surviving a wave while tethered awards 10 points. Harpooning a spirit pool awards 55 points per scatter.
energy_and_contribution.reward_permit_threshold: A successful encounter grants no permit below 2,000 personal points. At 2,000 points it grants one permit, then one additional permit for each complete 700 points above 2,000. Remaining points create a linearly scaled chance of one final additional permit.
energy_and_contribution.permit_storage: Up to 8,000 reward-pool rolls can be stored. Stored permits and claimed-permit count are player-observed counters; no permit balance is inferred from a run plan or activity history.
energy_and_contribution.success_boundary: The factual point formula and thresholds describe an observed result. A model must record successful completion, personal points, permit delta, and any XP only when supplied by the player or imported from a trusted account observation.

attacks_and_response.colossal_wave: A wave pushes untethered players and can destroy currently held minigame supplies. Tether to a mast or totem with rope, or the full Spirit angler set. Standing between ammunition crates avoids the push but not item loss. Waves extinguish fires and do not begin at 10 percent energy or lower. A tether site can break at a storm-intensity-scaled 15 to 25 percent chance and is repaired with a hammer.
attacks_and_response.lightning_and_fires: Lightning clouds start fires. Douse fires with bucket(s) of water; unattended fires spread. Waves extinguish fires. Lightning does not begin at 10 percent energy or lower, though existing fires can continue to spread.
attacks_and_response.torrent: A water torrent can disable a cannon temporarily and stun a player loading it. Step away or choose another cannon. Torrent does not begin at 10 percent energy or lower.
attacks_and_response.item_loss_and_death: These attacks do not normally deal player damage or create a grave/reclaim event. Only hammer, rope, bucket, bucket of water, raw harpoonfish, and harpoonfish may be destroyed by encounter attacks. All destroyed local tools can be replenished at cove crates; actual losses remain observed.

failure_and_death.failure: An unsuccessful encounter loses the points accrued in that encounter. It does not produce reward permits.
failure_and_death.player_combat_and_death: Tempoross is a skilling boss. Its described attacks hinder movement, disable cannons, create fires, and destroy limited minigame supplies rather than imposing a normal player death/reclaim loop. Treat an exceptional player death as a separately reported account event.
failure_and_death.recovery: Basic rope, bucket, hammer, and harpoon can be collected from cove crates. A previously carried special harpoon, outfit, spellbook state, or other account gear is not replaced or inferred by that local recovery.
failure_and_death.persistent_state: Observed reward permits, claimed-pool results, unique items, fish, pages, flakes, and collection-log entries persist. Temporary raw fish and local tools may be lost; neither their quantity nor loss event is assumed.

repeatability.round_entry: no stated GP fee, quest key, daily lockout, or consumable ticket

repeatability.daily_or_weekly_limit: none stated by current activity documentation

currencies.spend_behavior: Personal encounter score gates reward permits on successful completion. It is session-scoped: a failed encounter loses the accrued points. Record it only as a player-observed final/run value.

One permit is consumed for one Reward pool search. Whole successful-point thresholds are deterministic, while the final fractional permit is RNG. Existing shared production records call this currency tempoross-reward-permits; retain that canonical id during integration.

A Reward pool unique outcome gives 32 to 64 flakes at 1 in 4. Four exact 1,200-flake conversions plus observed corresponding Angler pieces can create the Spirit angler outfit. Do not infer flakes, purchases, or conversion state from searches.
currencies.drop_protection: No pity, threshold, or dry protection found. The 1,200-flake per-piece upgrade cost is deterministic only after observed flakes and the matching observed Angler piece.

currencies.spend_behavior: Reward-pool unique results supply pages. Pages charge a Tome of water and may replace duplicate Fish Barrel or Tackle Box reward slots in the quantities stated by the reward table.

logout_or_idle_constraints: Wave tethering, lightning fires, cannon disabling, fishing-spot movement, cooking/loading, and spirit-pool phases need active response.
A temporary no-special-attacks-at-10-percent-energy mechanic does not convert a complete encounter into a guaranteed low-attention activity.
Exact attention intervals, success, and actual mode are player- and rotation-observed rather than inferred from a guide.
afk_and_attention.source_boundary: Current mechanics sources establish reactive events. Community claims of lower-intensity solo methods are strategy candidates, not factual AFK classification.

community_strategy_observations.claim: Mass worlds can favor simpler group participation, while solo rotations can seek greater personal permit output by controlling energy, cooking, waves, and fires.
community_strategy_observations.boundary: No permits-per-hour, game duration, completion rate, or route preference is adopted. Group population, player inputs, equipment, execution, and current worlds vary.

community_strategy_observations.claim: The firefighter solo rotation intentionally manages fires and energy phases to increase reward-permit efficiency.
community_strategy_observations.boundary: The cited video declares advanced Fishing and Infernal harpoon assumptions for its shown route. It cannot establish universal readiness, expected permits, failure avoidance, or a recommended account stop.

community_strategy_observations.claim: Players sometimes save permits until base Fishing 81 to search under the highest documented Reward-pool bracket, while others open earlier for a possible Fish Barrel or harpoon.
community_strategy_observations.boundary: The level-at-claim rule is factual. Delaying searches, desired food mix, target Fishing level, and the value of earlier RNG opportunities are scoring decisions, not facts.

community_strategy_observations.claim: Fish Barrel is often treated by Ironman players as a utility target for later fishing loops, but it can be arbitrarily dry because it has no deterministic purchase path or pity protection.
community_strategy_observations.boundary: A future scoring model may value storage utility and opportunity cost, but must never issue a guaranteed permit, time, or stop recommendation from the 1-in-400 rate.

state_boundaries: Entry capability is distinct from current travel position, desert supplies, local tool possession, group selection, or a started encounter.

A successful game, personal points, permit delta, fractional-permit roll, XP, catches, Cooking/Construction/Strength outputs, local-tool loss, and failures are observed events, never implications of action:tempoross.
Reward permits are persistent only after observed successful threshold satisfaction. A failed encounter loses its points and cannot be converted into a permit later.
A Reward pool search consumes one observed permit and produces exactly one observed result. RNG rates establish availability, never ownership, count, or collection-log completion.
Fishing reward tiers use base Fishing at claim time; a temporary boost cannot select a higher tier and stored permits do not determine a tier before the search.
Unique item possession, collection-log confirmation, variants, Tome pages/charges, Fish Barrel contents/open state, and Tackle Box contents all require account observations.
Normal Tempoross attacks do not establish player death, grave, reclaim fee, combat-readiness state, or loss of account equipment outside the enumerated temporary/minigame items.
Sailing travel to Ruins of Unkah and any vessel state remain governed by the separate Sailing observations; this package only records it as an alternative transport path.

conflicts_and_unknowns.detail: Existing facts tempoross-fish-barrel, utility-tempoross-reward-permits, utility-tempoross-fish-barrel, and utility-stop-tempoross-fish-barrel remain authoritative current shared records. This package expands rather than replaces them; central integration must consolidate without duplicate canonical rates or source ids.

The Reward pool labels several rates as estimated from the Drop Rate Project sample set. Record the published current rates as sourced estimates and never turn them into deterministic expectations or pity calculations.

Normal cove tools are explicitly lost by encounter attacks. This package does not claim a global loss/protection rule for every special harpoon or Imcando hammer beyond the source-backed text included here. Any automatic lost-item/recovery logic needs item-specific facts.

Storm intensity, fishing spot timing, player count, pathing, food/cooking choice, special attacks, fire patterns, and wave responses make exact solo/group outputs execution-dependent. They belong to observations and future strategy scoring, not default fact transitions.

Fish Sack Barrel needs an observed Fish Barrel and Fish Sack. The Fish Sack's 1,000 Molch-pearl Aerial Fishing route is referenced by existing facts but not normalized here, avoiding an unrelated duplicate package.
